messages.subject: implementing direct boosting methodology
parts:
It seems that standard GBM have low performance when applied to insurance data sets (Poisson and Tweedie GBM)...
An alternative has been presented in current literature that appears to overcome such limitation issue:

Few references are: 

*http://actuaries.asn.au/Library/Events/ASTINAFIRERMColloquium/2015/AntonioEtAlDeltaBoostingPaper.pdf 
* https://www.casact.org/education/rpm/2013/handouts%5CPaper_1645_handout_874_0.pdf 

In particular a straight comparison of GBM and DBM is shown at page 19.

Probably its implementation could be quick and very useful when the outcome is rare and extremely skewed.
Do you think it would be possible to implement such modification?

Best
